useCase.name: Issue an official certificate to a student or an employee, filled from their record, and record the issue

intent.name: certificate.request
intent.summary: Raise a request for a certificate, for a student or an employee. One step, and nothing is issued by it.
routesHere: request a bonafide certificate — she needs it for a passport

routesHere.text: bonafide certificate chahiye, passport ke liye
routesHere.gloss: we need a bonafide certificate, for a passport

routesHere.text: character certificate ki darkhwast de do

routesHere.gloss: the employee needs an experience letter

routesHere: request a school leaving certificate for this student

request.text: offer letter chahiye
request.gloss: we need the offer letter

routesElsewhere.note: The offer letter is not one of these types. It is issued before an employee exists, filled from a candidate record, and has its own use case (BR-11, E7).

request.text: naam katwana hai
request.gloss: we want to withdraw the child

routesElsewhere.note: A withdrawal raises the certificate requests itself rather than leaving them to somebody to remember (BR-1, UC-03-06 BR-9).

request.text: certificate abhi chhap do
request.gloss: print the certificate now

routesElsewhere.note: The template is filled from the record and previewed before anything is printed (BR-3, BR-4).

steps.note: One step. Two other features raise the request themselves — a withdrawal and a staff exit — rather than leaving it to somebody to remember (BR-1).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A student type on an employee, an employee type on a student, and an appreciation certificate with no recognition behind it are all refused.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request and the audit entry together or not at all. Nothing is filled, printed or issued. Where a withdrawal makes release conditional on fee clearance and dues are outstanding, the request is held rather than refused (BR-8, E5).

operations.name: certificate.request
operations.idempotencyKey: person_id + certificate_type + purpose, since the same ask twice is one request
operations.purpose: Raise a certificate request for a confirmed person.

parameters.name: person_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No record matches, or the person is outside the actor's scope. A guardian requesting for a child who is not theirs is refused (E10).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, showing each candidate with their photograph, name, father's name, class and section or role, and identifier (BR-2).

parameters.notes: The student or employee, confirmed through the same person picker the card use case specifies (BR-2). A mistyped identifier resolves to a real record and produces a valid certificate for the wrong person.

parameters.name: certificate_type
parameters.type: enum: School leaving certificate | Character certificate | Bonafide or study certificate | Appreciation certificate | Experience or service letter | Dues clearance certificate
parameters.notes: What is being issued. Each applies to a student, an employee, or either — a student type cannot be issued to an employee, nor an employee type to a student (BR-3, E1, E2).

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.notes: Why the certificate is needed. Often required on the certificate itself, so it is the requester's own words rather than a purpose inferred from the type.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: person
fields.description: The confirmed person, as shown before confirmation (BR-2).

fields.name: requested_by
fields.description: Parent / Guardian, Student, Employee, Staff at the office, Withdrawal or Staff exit (BR-1).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Requested, or Held for clearance where a withdrawal makes release conditional and dues are outstanding (BR-8).

fields.name: held_for_clearance
fields.description: Whether release is being held. The condition applying at all is configuration (BR-8).

fields.name: previous_issues
fields.description: How many times this type has been issued to this person. A reissue produces a new certificate with its own number and both stay on the record (BR-9).

errors.meaning: A student type was selected for an employee.
errors.note: The template is filled from the student record and there is none (BR-3).

errors.meaning: An employee type was selected for a student.
An appreciation certificate was requested with no recognition behind it.
errors.note: It is the printed output of a recognition already recorded — a certificate praising something the school has no record of is one nobody can stand behind (BR-6).

errors.meaning: An offer letter was requested here.
errors.note: It is issued before an employee exists and has its own use case (BR-11).

errors.meaning: A guardian requested a certificate for a child who is not theirs.
Dues are outstanding and the withdrawal blocks the certificate.
errors.notWritten: It is held rather than issued (BR-8).
errors.note: Not a refusal. Report which document is held and what clears it.

planningRules.rule: Never select the type. Six types exist and each says something different about a person — a bonafide certificate and a character certificate are not interchangeable, and the wrong one is a document the next institution will reject.

Never confirm the person from a typed identifier alone. A mistyped one resolves to a real record and produces a valid certificate for the wrong person (BR-2), which is the same reasoning as the card use case.
Never write the purpose. It often appears on the certificate itself, so a purpose a planner supplied is the school stating why somebody needs a document.

Never request an appreciation certificate without the recognition. It is the printed output of one already recorded (BR-6, E6) — a certificate praising something the school has no record of is one nobody can stand behind.

Report a held certificate plainly, and say what clears it. Where a withdrawal makes release conditional on fee clearance, the document is held rather than refused (BR-8, E5) — and a held leaving certificate is a child who cannot enrol elsewhere.
Report previous issues of the same type. A reissue produces a new certificate with its own number and both stay on the record, so a school can see how many times a document was issued (BR-9).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A certificate is never deleted (BR-9, E8). A request that will not be issued is refused, and a reissue produces a new certificate with its own number.

request.text: bonafide certificate chahiye — passport banwana hai
request.gloss: we need a bonafide certificate — for a passport application

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, the student confirmed.

inputs.purpose: for a passport application, as the family said

steps.note: The type is the family's request and the purpose their own words (PR-1, PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Requested. Report that a bonafide certificate needs no withdrawal and no exit behind it — it is requested more often than every other type combined, and this is the ordinary route for it.

request.text: is bache ko certificate chahiye
request.gloss: this child needs a certificate

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, with no type named.

steps.note: No plan is emitted. The type is not inferred (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is requested. Ask which — a bonafide certificate for a bank or a passport, a character certificate, a leaving certificate, or the transcript. They say different things about a child, and the institution asking for one will not accept another.

request.text: mulazim ke liye offer letter jari kar do
request.gloss: issue the offer letter for the employee

steps.note: No plan is emitted here. The offer letter is not one of these types (PR governs via the routing).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is requested. Report that the appointment letter is issued before an employee exists, filled from the candidate record rather than a staff record, and has its own use case — this feature issues certificates to people the school already holds a record for.

intent.name: certificate.generate
intent.summary: Fill the certificate template from the person's own record and produce it for preview. One step, and nothing is issued yet.
routesHere: generate the certificate for this request

routesHere.text: is darkhwast ka certificate bana do
routesHere.gloss: generate the certificate for this request
fill the certificate from the record

routesHere.text: preview ke liye certificate tayyar karo

request.text: certificate par dastakhat karo
request.gloss: sign the certificate

request.text: khali khane khud bhar do
request.gloss: fill in the blank fields yourself

routesElsewhere.note: The template is filled from that person's record (BR-3). Where a field the template needs is missing, the certificate is not generated rather than being produced with a blank in it (E4).

steps.note: One step. The template is filled from the student record for a student type and the staff record for an employee type (BR-3), and printing happens from the preview so the filled document is seen before it is produced (BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A record missing a field the template needs produces nothing at all, rather than a certificate with a blank in it.
plan.atomicity: One write: the certificate, its number and the filled template together or not at all. It is not issued — signing and recording the issue are separate acts (BR-4, BR-5). Where a withdrawal makes release conditional on fee clearance and dues are outstanding, the request stays held and nothing is generated (BR-8).

operations.name: certificate.generate
operations.idempotencyKey: request_id, since a request generates one certificate
operations.purpose: Fill the certificate template from the person's record.

parameters.name: request_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No certificate request matches at a state that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the requests with the person, the type, who raised it and the status.

parameters.notes: The certificate request, resolved from the person and the type.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: source_record
fields.description: The student record for a student type, the staff record for an employee type (BR-3).

fields.name: fields_filled
fields.description: Every field, from that person's own record. None typed by hand (BR-3).

fields.name: signer_role
fields.description: The School Admin or the Principal, according to the type. Which types need which is an open question in this use case.

errors.meaning: The record is missing a field the template needs.
errors.note: Rather than being produced with a blank in it (E4). The message names the field.

errors.meaning: Dues are outstanding and the withdrawal blocks the certificate.
errors.note: It is held rather than issued (BR-8).

errors.meaning: An appreciation certificate has no recognition behind it.
errors.note: It is the printed output of one already recorded (BR-6).

planningRules.rule: Never supply a missing field. The template is filled from the person's own record (BR-3), and a value a planner produced is a statement the school is making about somebody in a document it signs.
Report the missing field by name where generation fails. It is a gap in the person's record, and somebody has to fill it there rather than on the certificate (E4).

Never describe a generated certificate as issued. Signing and recording the issue are separate acts, and printing happens from the preview so the filled document is seen before it is produced (BR-4, BR-5).
Report who signs, and that which types need which signature is undecided. The School Admin or the Principal signs according to the type, and nothing in this use case says which is which.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A certificate is never deleted (BR-9, E8). One generated in error is not issued, and a corrected one is generated as a reissue with its own number.

request.text: is darkhwast ka certificate bana do
request.gloss: generate the certificate for this request

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, on a bonafide request.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Generated and waiting at the preview. Report the certificate number and that it is not issued — it is signed and the issue recorded separately (PR-3), and printing happens from the preview so the filled document is seen first.

request.text: certificate bana do, walid ka naam record mein nahi hai to chhorh do
request.gloss: generate the certificate, and leave the father's name out since it is not on the record

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns MISSING_FIELD (E4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is generated. Report the missing field by name (PR-2) — it is filled on the student's record, not left blank on a document the school signs. A certificate with a gap where a name should be is one the next institution will query.

request.text: naam ki spelling theek kar ke certificate bana do
request.gloss: fix the spelling of the name and generate the certificate

steps.note: The generation only. Nothing on the record is changed (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that the certificate is filled from the record as it stands — if the spelling is wrong there, it is corrected on the record first and the certificate then generates correctly. Correcting it on the document alone would leave the record and the certificate saying different things about the same child.

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No certificate matches at a state that allows this.

planningRules.rule: Never record an issue that did not happen. This row is what a school answers with when asked what it issued and when (BR-5).
Report earlier issues of the same type. Both stay on the record and a reissue carries its own number, so the school can see how many times a document was issued (BR-9).

request.gloss: the family wants another copy, give them the same certificate again

steps.note: The same certificate is not issued twice. A reissue is a fresh request (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that a second copy is a reissue — a new request, a new certificate and a new number, with both staying on the record. That is how the school can later see a document was issued twice, which matters when two copies are in circulation.

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns HELD_FOR_CLEARANCE (E5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is issued. Report what is outstanding and that the hold lifts when the dues are cleared — and if the document is the school leaving certificate, that holding it is what stops the child enrolling anywhere else, which is a decision the school should be taking knowingly rather than as a side effect.

intent.name: certificate.hold.release
intent.summary: Lift a clearance hold once the dues are cleared. Accounts, one step.
routesHere: the dues are cleared — release the held certificate

routesElsewhere.note: A balance written off rather than collected goes through the write-off use case by the approver named there (UC-03-06 BR-6).

request.text: rok ke bawajood de do
request.gloss: give it despite the hold

routesElsewhere.note: The certificate is held rather than issued until the dues are cleared (BR-8, E5).

steps.note: One step. The dues are cleared and the hold lifts; the certificate is then generated, signed and issued as normal (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A hold on a request where dues are still outstanding does not lift.
plan.atomicity: One write: the hold lifted and the audit entry together or not at all. Nothing is generated or issued by it — the request returns to the ordinary path. Whether the clearance condition applies at all is configuration, and which way this school has it set is not stated anywhere in this use case (BR-8).

operations.name: certificate.hold.release
operations.idempotencyKey: request_id, since a hold lifts once
operations.purpose: Lift the clearance hold on a certificate request.

parameters.name: request_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No held certificate request matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the held requests with the person, the type and what is outstanding.

parameters.notes: The held certificate request, resolved from the person and the type.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Requested. It returns to the ordinary path (BR-8).

fields.name: dues_outstanding
fields.description: Zero, or what remains where the hold could not lift.

errors.meaning: The request is not held for clearance.

planningRules.rule: Never lift a hold with dues outstanding. E5 is BR-8 working, and lifting it is not how a balance is cleared.
Never write off a balance to lift a hold. That goes through the write-off use case by the approver named there — a certificate is not a route around it (UC-03-06 BR-6).
Report who has been waiting and for what. A held leaving certificate is a child who cannot enrol elsewhere, and the date the hold lifts is the date that stops being true.
Report that the certificate is not issued by this. The request returns to the ordinary path and is generated, signed and issued (BR-4, BR-5).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A lifted hold is not reimposed. Where dues arise again, that is a separate matter from a certificate already released.

request.text: baqaya ada ho gaya hai, rok hata do
request.gloss: the dues are paid, lift the hold

resolvedPlans.outcome: The hold lifts. Report who has been waiting and for which document (PR-3), and that it is now generated, signed and issued in the ordinary way (PR-4).

request.text: thora sa baqaya hai, phir bhi certificate release kar do
request.gloss: a small balance is left, release the certificate anyway

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns DUES_OUTSTANDING (E5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The hold does not lift. Report the balance. Worth adding that whether the school holds certificates on an outstanding balance at all is configuration, and whether it should hold the leaving certificate specifically is a question the withdrawal use case raises and does not answer — the document is what the child needs to enrol anywhere else.

request.text: baqaya maaf kar ke rok hata do
request.gloss: waive the balance and lift the hold

steps.note: No write-off is planned (PR-2). The hold lifts only once the balance is actually cleared.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing lifts. Report that the write-off is raised and approved under the write-off use case by the approver named there — clearing a balance to release a certificate would use a document the family needs as the reason to skip a financial control.
